lines.trans: Push with the heel of your hand, Ziad, fold once, quarter turn, push again!
Yes, Chef! How does the dough look now?
Smooth, soft, and springing right back—into the warm bowl under a damp cloth!
Four egg yolks, fresh lemon juice, and three spoons from the SUGAR jar, Salma!
Keep whisking over gentle heat, Nour—never let the bottom boil!
How is your ankle feeling this morning, Salma?
Honestly? Half the swelling is gone already because you two kept me off my feet!
Look how thick and glossy the yellow lemon curd just turned!
Off the flame immediately! Stir in one cold cube of unsalted butter!
Smell that bright lemon steam filling the whole ground floor!
Twenty crisp almond tart shells ready on the cooling tray!
Not bad at all, apprentices—my bakery is in safe hands!

Goodbye!

meanings.note: Reinforces negation to mean 'at all' or 'never'.

examples.trans: I didn't talk to him about the subject at all.

examples.text: الجو اليوم مو بارد أبداً، بالعكس دافي.
examples.trans: The weather today isn't cold at all; on the contrary, it's warm.

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: أرضية, plural: أرضيين).

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the ground floor.
The ground-floor rooms are close to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: صفرا, plural: صفر).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.
The yellow lemon cake is ready.

meanings.note: Feminine singular agreement for the non-human plural أيدي, meaning 'trustworthy/safe'.

examples.text: لا تخاف، مفاتيح البيت بأيدي أمينة.
examples.trans: Don't worry, the house keys are in safe hands.

examples.text: أبو سامي زلمة أمين والكل بيثق فيه.
examples.trans: Abu Sami is an honest man and everyone trusts him.

meanings.note: Strong spoken Levantine warning word meaning 'mind you don't / never!'.

examples.text: أوعى تنسى تطفي الغاز قبل ما تطلع!
examples.trans: Don't you dare forget to turn off the stove before you leave!

examples.text: أوعك تحكي لحد عن المفاجأة لسه.
examples.trans: Mind you don't tell anyone about the surprise yet.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Parts of the body in pairs are feminine in Arabic; 'my hands' is إيديي (iideyyi).

examples.trans: He washed his hands with warm water.
I planted the flowers with my own hand.

meanings.note: The universal relative pronoun in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: That is what I want.
The inn that keeps a stranger's bag safe.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: باردة, plural: باردين).

examples.trans: Here, drink a glass of cold water.
My hands were cold from the rain.

meanings.note: Noun for steam or vapour.

examples.text: البخار طالع من طنجرة الشوربة ومغبّش الشباك.
examples.trans: Steam is rising from the soup pot and fogging up the window.

examples.text: عملت بخار لقميصي قبل المقابلة عشان يطلع مرتب.
examples.trans: I steamed my shirt before the interview so it would look neat.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'without', used identically to MSA.

examples.text: شاي أحمر بدون سكر لو سمحتي.
examples.trans: Black tea without sugar, please.
I entered the booking without my glasses!

meanings.note: Most often heard in understated Jordanian praise: مش بطال ('not bad at all!').

examples.trans: Not bad for a first week of work!
The weather today is not bad at all.

meanings.note: Collective plural بيض ('eggs'), singulative بيضة ('one egg'), dual بيضتين ('two eggs').

examples.trans: I fried two eggs for breakfast.
Hot eggs are delicious with bread.

meanings.note: Baked fruit or custard tart, especially تارت الليمون ('lemon tart').

examples.text: تارت الليمون بقشرة اللوز طلع أطيب واحد.
examples.trans: The lemon tart with the almond crust turned out to be the tastiest one.

examples.text: خلينا قطعة تارت صغيرة لطارق بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We saved a small slice of tart for Tariq in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Form II verbal noun of برّد (to cool down).

examples.text: التبريد بالمخزن شغال منيح عشان الخضرة ما تخرب.
examples.trans: The cooling in the storeroom is working well so the vegetables don't spoil.

examples.text: سيب الكيكة تبرد عالرف، التبريد بياخد نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Let the cake cool on the rack; cooling takes half an hour.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: جاهزة, plural: جاهزين).

examples.trans: The desk is clean and the keys are ready.
Breakfast is ready in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Active participle of حسّ (to feel); Arabic uses participles for current sensations.

examples.text: حاسة حالي تعبانة شوي بعد المشوار الطويل.
examples.trans: I'm feeling a bit tired after the long walk.

examples.text: حاسّ إنو في إشي حلو رح يصير اليوم.
examples.trans: I have a feeling something nice is going to happen today.

meanings.note: Polite everyday reply meaning 'yes / at your service / right away'.

examples.text: حاضر يا ستي، دقيقتين وبجيبلك كاسة المي.
examples.trans: Right away, ma'am—two minutes and I'll bring you a glass of water.

examples.text: لا تشيل هم، حاضر، بمر عالبنك عنك.
examples.trans: Don't worry—consider it done, I'll stop by the bank for you.

meanings.note: With possessive endings, حال acts as 'myself/yourself/itself' (لحاله by itself, لا تغلبي حالك don't tire yourself).

examples.trans: The door opened by itself from the wind.
How are you doing today?

meanings.note: Form II verb حرّك means 'to move' or 'to stir' ingredients.

examples.text: حرّك الشوربة منيح عشان ما تلزق بقاع الطنجرة.
examples.trans: Stir the soup well so it doesn't stick to the bottom of the pot.

examples.text: لا تحرّك الطاولة وأنا عم بلزق الورق.
examples.trans: Don't move the table while I'm gluing the paper.

meanings.note: Culinary verb for whisking eggs, lemon curd, or cream until smooth.

examples.text: نور بتخفق البيض مع الليمون والسكر بهدوء.
examples.trans: Nour whisks the eggs gently with lemon and sugar.

examples.text: خفقت سلمى الكريمة حتى صارت ناعمة ومتساوية.
examples.trans: Salma whisked the curd until it turned smooth and glossy.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: Used to describe warm weather, warm water, or a cozy feeling.

examples.trans: The bread is warm and fresh from the oven.
Sitting in the attic is cozy when it rains.

meanings.note: Common everyday verb for 'went' in the past tense. Also used as a future particle.

examples.trans: We missed our chance — he hung up!

examples.text: كل التعب راح مع أول فنجان قهوة.
examples.trans: All the tiredness vanished with the first cup of coffee.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أرباع.

examples.trans: Breakfast is at seven fifteen in the morning.
I will be back in fifteen minutes.

رجع.gloss: to return; come back; start again

meanings.en: to return; come back; start again
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (برجع, بيرجع).

examples.trans: Can you run there and come back in ten minutes?
Did the pipe start dripping again?

meanings.note: Feminine body-part noun in Levantine Arabic (رجلك اليمين 'your right foot').

examples.text: ارفعي رجلك عالمخدة وارتاحي نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Prop your foot up on the pillow and rest for half an hour.

examples.text: حطيت كيس تلج ملفوف بمنشفة على رجلي.
examples.trans: I placed an ice pack wrapped in a towel on my foot.

meanings.note: Everyday word for butter. Metaphorically means 'the essence' or 'bottom line'.

examples.text: بدي خبز سخن مع شوية زبدة.
examples.trans: I would like warm bread with a little butter.
Is this salted butter or unsalted?

meanings.note: Male given name, here referring to Rami's older brother.

examples.text: زياد بيساعد أخوه الصغير بحسابات المقهى.
examples.trans: Ziad helps his younger brother with the café's accounts.

examples.text: اسأل زياد وين حط الفواتير الشهرية.
examples.trans: Ask Ziad where he put the monthly invoices.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: I like black tea without sugar.
We sprinkled powdered sugar over the cake.

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Female given name belonging to the café's morning baker.

examples.text: سلمى بتخبز الكرواسون والخبز كل يوم الفجر.
examples.trans: Salma bakes the croissants and bread every day at dawn.

examples.text: سلمى جابت صينية كعك طازة للضيوف.
examples.trans: Salma brought a tray of fresh cookies for the guests.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

شال.gloss: to carry away; remove; lift out

meanings.en: to carry away; remove; lift out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بشيل, بيشيل).

examples.text: بنقدر نشيل أربع صناديق بخمس دقايق.
examples.trans: We can move four boxes in five minutes.
Sparkling water lifts the stain right out.

meanings.note: Feminine imperative of شمّ (to smell), addressing Salma.

examples.text: شمّي ريحة القرفة والهيل طالعة من الفرن!
examples.trans: Smell the scent of cinnamon and cardamom coming out of the oven!

examples.text: بحب أشمّ هوا نضيف بالحديقة الصبح.
examples.trans: I love breathing in fresh air in the garden in the morning.

meanings.note: Used across modern Jordanian kitchens and cafés for both male and female head chefs.

examples.text: الدفتر جاهز يا شيف سلمى، بشو نبلش؟
examples.trans: The clipboard is ready, Chef Salma—what do we start with?

examples.text: الشيف ذاق الشوربة وابتسم من أول معلقة.
examples.trans: The chef tasted the soup and smiled from the very first spoonful.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Everyday word for both a dinner plate and a teacup saucer (صحن الفنجان).

examples.text: رتبت سلمى اتنعش صحن أبيض جنب الفناجين.
examples.trans: Salma arranged twelve white saucers next to the cups.

examples.text: حطي الكيك السخن بصحن كبير عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Put the warm cake on a big plate on the table.

meanings.note: Used constantly as بصراحة or bare صراحة ('honestly / to be frank').

examples.trans: Honestly, I loved the place very much.
Frankly, the coffee here is excellent.

meanings.note: Literally 'yellowness', used in Arabic kitchens for egg yolk.

examples.text: ادهن وجه الفطاير بصفار البيض عشان تطلع دهبية.
examples.trans: Brush the top of the pastries with egg yolk so they turn golden.

examples.text: افصل صفار البيض عن البياض قبل ما تخفقه.
examples.trans: Separate the egg yolk from the white before whipping it.

meanings.note: Broken plural صواني ('serving trays' or 'oven baking pans').

examples.text: جهزنا تلات صواني خبز عشان تدخل الفرن الفجر.
examples.trans: We prepped three trays of bread to go into the oven at dawn.

examples.text: نور حملت صينية الشاي بالنعنع للساحة.
examples.trans: Nour carried the mint tea tray out to the courtyard.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian verb ضلّ (to keep/stay), used before another verb to mean 'keep on doing'.

examples.text: ضلّ عم بتدرّب، صوتك عم بتحسن كل يوم!
examples.trans: Keep practicing—your voice is getting better every day!

examples.text: ما ضلّ قهوة بالعلبة، لازم نشتري بكرا.
examples.trans: There's no coffee left in the tin; we have to buy some tomorrow.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

meanings.note: Used for fresh food, produce, or bread.

examples.text: خبز سلمى طازة وسخن كل صبح.
examples.trans: Salma's bread is fresh and hot every morning.

examples.text: اشترينا ليمون طازة ونعنع أخضر من السوق.
examples.trans: We bought fresh lemons and green mint from the market.

meanings.note: Everyday food adjective for soft, tender bread or fresh dough.

examples.text: الخبز الطالع من الفرن لسه سخن وطري كتير.
examples.trans: The bread coming out of the oven is still hot and very soft.

examples.text: اعجن العجينة منيح لحد ما تصير طرية ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: Knead the dough well until it becomes soft and cohesive.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطوي, بيطوي).

examples.trans: Fold this sheet and put it in your pocket.
She folded the clean towels in the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday baking noun for dough or batter, from عجن (to knead).

examples.text: غطّي العجين بمنشفة نضيفة وخليه يرتاح نص ساعة.
examples.trans: Cover the dough with a clean towel and let it rest for half an hour.

examples.text: ريحة العجين المخمّر بالمخبز بتفتح النفس.
examples.trans: The smell of fermented dough in the bakery whets your appetite.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصاير.

examples.trans: Fresh orange juice is cold and tasty.
I poured two glasses of juice for breakfast.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: Everyday kitchen verb for boiling liquids.

examples.text: بس تغلي المي، وطّي الغاز وحط الشاي.
examples.trans: Once the water boils, turn down the stove and put in the tea.

examples.text: الحليب غلى وفار عالغاز لأني سهيت عنه.
examples.trans: The milk boiled and overflowed on the stove because I got distracted.

meanings.note: Crisp adverb meaning 'at once / immediately', ending in adverbial tanwin -an.

examples.text: بس سمعت الخبر طلعت من البيت فوراً.
examples.trans: As soon as I heard the news, I left the house immediately.

examples.text: إذا في أي مشكلة بالطلب، خبرني فوراً.
examples.trans: If there's any issue with the order, let me know right away.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Refers to the bottom of a pot, pan, or valley.

examples.text: المفتاح وقع في قاع الشنطة تحت الكتب.
examples.trans: The key fell to the bottom of the bag underneath the books.

examples.text: انتبه لا ينحرق الرز بقاع الطنجرة.
examples.trans: Be careful not to let the rice burn at the bottom of the pot.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word from قد إيه ('how much / how very'), used in exclamations.

examples.text: قديه حق هاد الصحن الخزف لو سمحت؟
examples.trans: How much does this ceramic plate cost, please?

examples.text: قديه حلوة القعدة هون تحت شجرة الليمون!
examples.trans: How lovely it is sitting here under the lemon tree!

meanings.note: Singulative of collective قشر ('peel, bark, shell'); قشرة الليمونة means 'the skin/zest of the lemon'.

examples.text: قشرة الليمون الأصفر ريحتها قوية وحلوة.
examples.trans: Yellow lemon peel has a strong, sweet scent.

examples.text: بتحط سلمى برش قشرة ليمون بعجينة الكيك.
examples.trans: Salma puts grated lemon peel into the cake batter.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Anatomical and everyday word for 'ankle' (كاحلي اليمين 'my right ankle').

examples.text: الحمد لله كاحلي مش وارم، بس بده راحة.
examples.trans: Thankfully my ankle isn't swollen—it just needs rest.

examples.text: حطينا تلج عالكاحل ربع ساعة وخف الوجع.
examples.trans: We put ice on the ankle for fifteen minutes and the ache eased.

meanings.note: The Amman verb for pressing a button, doorbell or switch.

examples.text: اكبس الزر الأحمر عشان يفتح الباب.
examples.trans: Press the red button to open the door.

examples.text: كبست الجرس مرتين وما حدا فتح.
examples.trans: I pressed the bell twice and nobody opened.

meanings.note: Culinary noun used for كريمة الليمون ('lemon curd / cream') and pastry fillings.

examples.text: نور جهزت كريمة الليمون الصفرا للتارت.
examples.trans: Nour prepared the bright yellow lemon curd for the tarts.

examples.text: ريحة كريمة الليمون الطازة عبت المطبخ كله.
examples.trans: The aroma of fresh lemon curd filled the entire kitchen.

meanings.note: Names the heel of a foot or shoe (كعب القدم / كعب الحذاء).

examples.text: زحلق كعب حذائي عن حرف الطبلية الواطية.
examples.trans: The heel of my shoe slipped off the edge of the low stool.

examples.text: اسندي كعبك عالوسادة الطرية عشان ترتاح رجلك.
examples.trans: Rest your heel on the soft cushion so your foot can relax.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: The main interrogative word for asking about manner or state.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?
Tell me how to find the shop.

meanings.note: Takes pronoun suffixes in spoken Jordanian: لأني (because I), لأنك (because you), لأنه (because he/it — also general 'because'), لأنكم (because you pl.).

examples.text: لأنه القهوة الطيبة بتخلي الناس لطاف!
examples.trans: Because good coffee makes people pleasant!
Thank you because you kept the bag safe.

meanings.note: Used in Jordan to mean a wrap or a sandwich (e.g. falafel or shawarma), or a turn in the road.

examples.text: أكلت لفة قرفة سخنة مع الشاي.
examples.trans: I ate a warm cinnamon roll with tea.
Watch the tight turn on the stairs.

meanings.note: Imperative of لفّ (to turn, wrap, or rotate).

examples.text: لفّ على اليمين بعد الإشارة التانية بتلاقي المخبز.
examples.trans: Turn right after the second traffic light and you'll find the bakery.

examples.text: لفّ الساندويش بورق الزبدة عشان يضل سخن.
examples.trans: Wrap the sandwich in parchment paper so it stays warm.

meanings.en: to shine; to gleam; to sparkle
meanings.note: Sound Form I verb (بلمع / لمعت) from root ل-م-ع, used for polished metal or bright ink.

examples.trans: The drawings still shine on the paper.
The brass lock gleamed in the sun.

meanings.note: Literally means almonds, but heavily used in Jordanian youth slang to mean 'everything is perfect' or 'great'.

examples.text: ريحة اللوز المحمص طالعة من فرن سلمى.
examples.trans: The aroma of toasted almonds is drifting out of Salma's oven.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز بتعطي تارت الليمون قرمشة طيبة.
examples.trans: An almond crust gives the lemon tart a delicious crunch.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: ليمون.

examples.trans: The warm lemon cake is ready.
I squeezed half a lemon into the soup.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مبلولة, plural: مبلولين).

examples.trans: The wet wood on the shutters softens the echo.
His coat was wet from the rain.

meanings.note: From بيّن (to appear/seem); asks how something looks right now.

examples.text: مبيّن عليك التعب اليوم، ما نمت منيح مبارح؟
examples.trans: You look tired today—didn't you sleep well last night?

examples.text: السما مبيّنة صافية اليوم وما في غيم.
examples.trans: The sky looks clear today and there aren't any clouds.

meanings.note: Plural of متدرّب (trainee/apprentice), from تدرّب (to train).

examples.text: في متدرّب جديد عم بتعلم شغل الحلويات مع سلمى.
examples.trans: There's a new apprentice learning pastry work with Salma.
The trainees at the company helped set up the exhibition.

meanings.note: Noun of place from خبز (to bake), with -ي ('my').

examples.text: ريحة الخبز الطازة طالعة من مخبز الحارة من الساعة ستة.
examples.trans: The smell of fresh bread has been wafting out of the neighborhood bakery since six.

examples.text: فتحت مخبزي الصغير بهالشارع قبل تلات سنين.
examples.trans: I opened my small bakery on this street three years ago.

meanings.note: 'Marrah' means 'a time/once' (e.g. waḥdeh marrah = one time), but 'mara' (مَرَة) means 'woman/wife' in colloquial Jordanian.

examples.trans: The doorbell rang twice.
I read the letter three times.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine pantry word (also pronounced مرطبان) for glass storage jars (dual مرتبانين).

examples.text: حطيت مرتبانين قزاز كبار عالرف: واحد سكر وواحد ملح.
examples.trans: I put two big glass jars on the shelf: one sugar and one salt.

examples.text: لزقنا ملصق واضح على كل مرتبان بالمطبخ.
examples.trans: We stuck a clear label onto every jar in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Levantine active participle of عبّى (to fill), functioning like an ongoing verb.

examples.text: الورد معبّي الحوش ألوان وريحة حلوة بالربيع.
examples.trans: The flowers are filling the courtyard with colors and lovely scent in spring.

examples.text: أبوي معبّي الكرتونة كتب قديمة عشان نتبرع فيها.
examples.trans: My dad has filled the box with old books to donate.

meanings.note: Spoken Levantine metathesis of ملعقة ('spoon'), placing the ع before the ل.

examples.text: حطّي معلقة صغيرة قرفة على وجه السحلب.
examples.trans: Put a teaspoon of cinnamon on top of the sahlab.

examples.text: نسيت أجيب المعلقة عشان أحرك الشاي فيها.
examples.trans: I forgot to bring the spoon to stir the tea with.

meanings.note: Favorite Levantine food word for crusty fresh bread or crisp pastry.

examples.text: الخبز طلع من الفرن سخن ومقرمش.
examples.trans: The bread came out of the oven hot and crusty.

examples.text: قشرة اللوز المقرمشة أطيب إشي بالتارت.
examples.trans: The crisp almond crust is the best part of the tart.

meanings.note: Used for ice cubes (مكعب تلج), sugar cubes, and diced vegetables.

examples.text: دوق الشوربة وشوف إذا بدها كمان مكعب جزر.
examples.trans: Taste the soup and see if it needs another cube of carrot.

examples.text: لفينا مكعبات التلج بمنشفة قطن نضيفة.
examples.trans: We wrapped the ice cubes in a clean cotton towel.

meanings.note: Essential kitchen noun; ملح بحر = 'sea salt'.

examples.text: إوعك تخربط بين مرتبان السكر ومرتبان الملح!
examples.trans: Don't ever mix up the sugar jar and the salt jar!

examples.text: حطيت نص معلقة ملح بالعجين قبل الخبز.
examples.trans: I added half a spoonful of salt to the dough before baking.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Active participle from أنعش (to refresh); naturally captures bright, zesty citrus aroma.

examples.text: عصير الليمون بالنعنع مشروب منعش كتير بالصيف.
examples.trans: Lemon-mint juice is a very refreshing drink in the summer.

examples.text: الهوا الصبح عالبلكونة كان بارد ومنعش.
examples.trans: The morning air on the balcony was cool and crisp.

meanings.note: Common Levantine variant of مش used to negate adjectives and nouns.

examples.text: الجو اليوم مو بارد كتير متل مبارح.
examples.trans: The weather today isn't as cold as yesterday.

examples.text: هادي الشنطة مو إلي، اسأل مازن إذا لإلو.
examples.trans: This bag isn't mine—ask Mazen if it's his.

meanings.note: Feminine noun (unmarked, without ة ending). Used both for campfires and a kitchen stove flame.

examples.trans: The kitchen stove fire is still a bit low.
Put the kettle on the fire.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين); سكر ناعم means 'powdered sugar'.

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Appears in صباح النور ('morning of light', the standard reply to صباح الخير) and نور الشمس ('sunlight').

examples.trans: Good morning and welcome!
We read the card in the sunlight.

meanings.note: Masculine هادي ('quiet') is homographic with the feminine demonstrative هادي ('this'); context and agreement distinguish them cleanly.

examples.trans: The spot above the tree is very quiet.
We prepared the quiet attic room for you.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Medical/everyday noun for swelling or a bump.

examples.text: حطّيت ثلج على إيدي عشان يخفّ الورم بسرعة.
examples.trans: I put ice on my hand so the swelling would go down quickly.

examples.text: صار في ورم خفيف برجله بعد ما التوى كاحله.
examples.trans: There was a slight swelling in his foot after he twisted his ankle.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بوقف, بيوقف).

examples.trans: A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate!
My heart stopped at page one!

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!

meanings.note: Standard noun for day, often used in expressions like 'el-yom' (today).

examples.trans: Today the weather is sunny and warm in Amman.
Have a happy, successful day!
